overview: CDW Corporation is a Fortune 500, multi-brand reseller and integrator of IT hardware, software, and services to business, government, education, and healthcare customers across the US, UK, and Canada. The company sits in the middle of the IT value chain, procuring more than 100,000 products from over 1,000 vendor partners (Dell, HP, Cisco, Microsoft, Apple, Lenovo, Nvidia, etc.) and wholesale distributors, then adding value through configuration, integration, advisory, and managed services for over 250,000 customers. Effective January 1, 2026, CDW realigned from Corporate/Small Business/Public segments to Commercial/Government/Education segments, with CDW UK and CDW Canada reported as 'Other'.

business_model.summary: CDW buys IT hardware, software, and cloud/subscription products at scale and resells them with value-added integration and services, earning a gross margin spread (historically ~21-22%, compressed to ~20.5% in 2026 amid an AI-hardware mix shift) rather than owning IP. Transactional/project-based hardware and software sales are the majority of revenue, supplemented by a smaller but growing base of recurring, higher-margin services (advisory, managed services, cloud, warranties).

revenue_streams.name: Hardware (notebooks, netcomm, data storage/servers, desktops, other)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - commercial enterprise and SMB, plus government, healthcare, and education institutions; ~90% of net sales from the US, remainder from UK and Canada
business_model.geographic_mix: US ~90%, UK and Canada combined ~10% (FY2025: $2.7 billion from UK/Canada)

main_competitors: Hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Marketplace)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest US-focused IT solutions reseller/integrator by revenue (~$22.4B net sales FY2025) in a highly fragmented market served by thousands of resellers; roughly 2-3x the revenue of its closest public peer, Insight Enterprises (~$8.2B)

moat_factors.description: Two North America and one UK distribution center shipping ~22 million units annually; scale enables investment in specialists/engineers that smaller VARs cannot match
Highest-tier certifications with Cisco, Dell, HPE, Microsoft, Nutanix, Palo Alto Networks, etc., granting favorable pricing, incentive programs, and product access

250,000+ customers across diversified end-markets (corporate, SMB, government, education, healthcare) with long-tenured account managers (50%+ of US sales from reps with 7+ years tenure), but individual purchases are largely re-biddable
Being technology/vendor-unbiased lets CDW tailor solutions across competing OEMs, a value-add versus single-vendor resellers

weaknesses: Thin gross margins (~20-22%) leave earnings highly sensitive to product/customer mix shifts
No proprietary IP or hardware - commoditized reseller economics susceptible to direct-to-customer sales by OEMs and cloud providers
Heavy dependence on a handful of vendor partners (Apple, Cisco, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft) and two wholesale distributors (Ingram Micro, TD SYNNEX, >25% of purchases) for product access and terms
Growing hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Marketplace) could disintermediate traditional resellers over time
Gross margin compression in 2026 from AI-hardware mix shift (lower-margin servers/storage growing faster than higher-margin software/services)

growth_drivers: AI-driven data center/infrastructure refresh cycle - data storage and servers sales nearly doubled YoY in Q3 2026, pulling overall hardware growth to +21%
Expansion of higher-margin services and solutions capabilities (Digital Velocity, cloud migration, security, data/AI consulting) via organic investment and tuck-in M&A

Acquisitions deepening cloud/AI/data capabilities: Mission Cloud Services (Dec 2024, AWS Premier Tier Partner) and Lovelytics (closed Sept 25, 2026, $525M, Databricks-focused data/AI consultancy with 600+ staff)
New ERP system and broader transformation initiatives expected to streamline operations and improve productivity through 2026
Segment realignment (Commercial/Government/Education, effective Jan 1, 2026) intended to sharpen go-to-market focus on growth verticals including financial services and healthcare
Continued capital return program - raised share buyback authorization ($1 billion increase announced May 2026) and 8% dividend increase (to $0.68/share) announced November 2026

Secular IT spending growth expected to outpace GDP, driven by cloud, hybrid infrastructure, security, and AI adoption across a highly fragmented reseller market where CDW can continue consolidating share

business.description: Significant sales derived from Apple, Cisco, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft; >25% of purchases from Ingram Micro and TD SYNNEX combined - loss of or adverse changes to any relationship could hurt margins and supply

business.risk: Gross margin compression from AI hardware mix
business.description: Fast growth in lower-margin data storage/server sales (AI infrastructure) is diluting blended gross margin (20.5% in Q3 2026 vs 21.9% a year earlier)
Vendors increasingly sell direct or through hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS/Google/Microsoft Marketplace), potentially reducing the traditional reseller's role and pressuring margins
CDW extends credit for a large share of sales; a shift toward multi-year subscription billing is lengthening DSO (100 days as of Sept 2026 vs 92 a year earlier)

financial.description: Total unsecured debt grew to $7.1 billion by Q3 2026 (from $5.6B) after new notes issuance (5.70%-6.35% coupons) partly to fund the Lovelytics acquisition; net debt $5.6B; interest expense up ~20% YoY
GBP and CAD exposure from CDW UK/Canada operations can swing reported results
A portion of borrowings are at variable rates, exposing CDW to higher debt service costs if rates rise

regulatory.risk: DOJ False Claims Act investigation (E-Rate program)
regulatory.description: DOJ issued a Civil Investigative Demand in June 2024 regarding bids for Schools and Libraries Program (E-Rate) contracts; outcome and potential liability remain unresolved as of the FY2025 10-K
Government, education, and healthcare contracts carry termination-for-convenience, procurement regulation, and GPO-access risk; government shutdowns can delay funding and purchases
Evolving AI regulation could raise compliance costs and create liability as CDW embeds AI in its offerings and operations

macro.description: Customer technology budgets are discretionary and sensitive to economic conditions, interest rates, and inflation; customers can defer purchases during uncertainty
US government shutdowns and shifting federal budget priorities can delay or reduce public sector, education, and healthcare technology spending
Vendor partners manufacture heavily in Asia; new tariffs, export controls, or trade restrictions could raise costs or constrain supply
Tightening memory/storage supply as OEMs prioritize datacenter/AI workloads is lengthening lead times and raising prices for commercial devices and servers

macro_factors.industry_outlook: IT spending is expected to outpace general economic growth, driven by cloud/hybrid computing, cybersecurity, and AI adoption; the US/UK/Canada reseller market remains large, growing, and highly fragmented (thousands of competitors), supporting continued consolidation by scaled players like CDW
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - IT hardware/software spending is discretionary and can be deferred in downturns, though diversified end-markets (government, healthcare, education act as stabilizers) dampen volatility relative to pure-play consumer tech
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - CDW carries meaningful debt ($7.1B total, with a variable-rate portion) and extends customer credit; higher rates raise both CDW's borrowing costs and customers' propensity to delay IT purchases
key_input_costs: Semiconductors/memory and storage components (acute AI-driven tightness)
Hardware costs from OEMs (Dell, HP, Lenovo, etc.)
Labor costs for specialists and engineers

recent_developments.event: Net sales of $6.75 billion, up 17.7% YoY, beat consensus ($6.19B); adjusted EPS of $3.26 beat consensus ($2.98); stock rose 12.7% on the day, closing at a 52-week high of $168.75
Management raised FY2026 non-GAAP EPS growth guidance to 'low double-digit' from 'high single-digit' previously, citing orders outpacing invoicing and a building backlog
Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.68/share (up ~8% from $0.63), payable December 10, 2026

Completed acquisition of Lovelytics (Databricks-focused data/AI consultancy, ~600 employees across US/Canada/Argentina/Colombia) for a base purchase price of $525 million plus ~$44 million in restricted stock
Issued $1.5 billion of new senior notes (5.70% due 2029, 6.10% due 2032, 6.35% due 2033) partly to refinance 2026 maturities and fund the Lovelytics deal
Board authorized a $1 billion increase to the share repurchase program
Realigned reportable segments from Corporate/Small Business/Public to Commercial/Government/Education, effective for periods beginning Q1 2026

AI-driven demand for data storage and servers nearly doubled YoY through the first nine months of 2026, becoming the primary hardware growth driver, while gross margin compressed ~70-140 bps YoY due to the lower-margin mix shift
Acquired Mission Cloud Services, a leading US-based AWS Premier Tier Partner, to build out CDW's dedicated AWS practice
Received a DOJ Civil Investigative Demand regarding E-Rate (Schools and Libraries Program) bid practices; matter remains open as of the FY2025 10-K

items.notes: Raised from prior 'high single-digit' growth guidance following a strong Q3 beat and AI-driven hardware demand
Management characterized demand momentum as building into year-end, driven by AI infrastructure and data center investment
Approximately 8% increase from the prior $0.63 quarterly rate
5.3 million shares repurchased for $653 million in the first nine months of 2026; ~$1+ billion remained available as of Q3 2026 after the increase

guidance.management_commentary: Management attributed the Q3 beat to broad-based demand across all operating segments, with AI-related data storage and server investment as the standout driver (hardware sales +21%, data storage/servers nearly doubling YoY). Gross margin compression (20.5% vs 21.9% a year ago) was attributed to mix shift into large, hardware-heavy AI infrastructure projects, which management framed as a trade-off for strong top-line and backlog growth rather than a structural deterioration.

bull_case: AI infrastructure build-out is driving outsized hardware demand (data storage/servers nearly doubling YoY), positioning CDW as a key channel partner capturing enterprise AI capex

Raised FY2026 guidance (low double-digit EPS growth) and a building order backlog suggest momentum carrying into 2027, with the Q3 2026 beat and +12.7% stock reaction reflecting renewed investor confidence
Services/data-AI capability build-out (Mission Cloud, Lovelytics) diversifies the business toward higher-margin, stickier recurring revenue and reduces pure hardware-reseller cyclicality over time

Consistent capital return discipline - dividend raised ~8% and buyback authorization increased by $1 billion in 2026 - signals management confidence and supports EPS growth even if top-line growth moderates
Scale advantages (distribution, vendor certifications, 250,000+ diversified customers) and a highly fragmented competitive market leave room for continued share gains versus smaller VARs
bear_case: Gross margin structurally pressured by mix shift toward lower-margin AI hardware (data storage/servers); if this mix persists, blended margins may not recover to prior 21-22% levels
Rising leverage (total debt grew from $5.6B to $7.1B in 2026, partly debt-funded M&A) and higher interest expense (+20% YoY) increase financial risk if IT spending growth slows
Thin reseller economics leave CDW vulnerable to disintermediation from OEMs selling direct and growing hyperscaler marketplaces (AWS/Google/Microsoft), which could erode its channel role over time
Open DOJ False Claims Act investigation into E-Rate bidding practices carries unresolved legal/financial/reputational risk, particularly given CDW's reliance on public sector and education contracts

Government, healthcare, and education spending (meaningful share of revenue) remains exposed to budget uncertainty, funding delays, and government shutdown risk, which could offset commercial-side AI tailwinds
